paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take home. John had every reason to make himself the main act. The crowds came, the priests came, and a whole delegation showed up asking, "Who are you?" He said, "I am not the Christ." Then he gave them a job description instead of a title: "I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, 'Make straight the way for the Lord.'" (John 1:20, 23)

A voice isn't the point. It's there to point at somebody else. John's whole life was a finger aimed at Jesus, and when the day came, he said it plain: "Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" (John 1:29) Think about that, baker. The One who stands above John, whose sandal straps John says he isn't worthy to untie (John 1:27), is the One who carries away the sin of the world.

And John didn't just say it, he testified to what he had seen: the Spirit coming down like a dove and resting on Jesus, and "this is the Son of God." (John 1:32, 34) That's what I want you holding when you walk out of my bakery. You don't have to be the star of the batch. Your job is to point people to Jesus, and I'll tell you, that's a GREAT job to have.
